notes.title: Gauntlet Changelog Still Identifies v1.0.1 as Current
notes.problem: The selected current world is The Gauntlet v1.0.2 and both behavior/resource pack manifests identify version 1.0.2, while the Drive changelog still states v1.0.1 is the current version.
notes.action: Update the changelog/version documentation to identify v1.0.2 as the current release and preserve the older entries as history.

notes.title: Explicitly Own the Gauntlet World Gamerule Baseline
notes.problem: The production world setup explicitly normalizes only a limited gamerule set. The map has scripted combat, building/breaking and custom recovery, so leaving relevant world-interaction rules implicit increases the chance that imported/world-edited state changes gameplay unexpectedly.
notes.action: Review and explicitly set every Gauntlet-specific gameplay-relevant gamerule in the map's existing world-setup owner, including mob griefing, mob/entity/tile drops, fire tick and projectile block breaking where compatible with authored mechanics. Re-verify that same baseline at safe lifecycle boundaries such as world bootstrap/session start rather than relying on prior world state. Do not create a second gamerule authority. Keep doImmediateRespawn only after the Level 6 recovery race is fixed and verified.

evidence.relatedRuntimeFinding: Level 6 lethal Dropper failure can enter native immediate-respawn and custom recovery concurrently.

notes.title: Clarify Operator Versus Developer Authority for Gauntlet Script Events
notes.problem: Several developer script-event handlers rely on command/operator access but do not consistently re-check the Gauntlet internal developer permission before mutating progression or arena state.
notes.action: Define whether Roommaster/operator authority is intentionally equivalent to Gauntlet Developer. If not, route all developer script-event mutations through the existing internal developer-permission owner. Do not change behavior until that authority decision is explicit.

notes.title: Keep Hunger Stable During Active Gauntlet Runs
notes.problem: Tester runtime shows hunger can decrease during an active run and affect sprint/movement even though the selected artifact does not establish hunger as an intended challenge mechanic.
notes.action: Decide and implement the intended active-run hunger policy. If hunger is not part of the design, maintain sufficient hunger/saturation throughout the run and reassert it after retry, level transition, reconnect and respawn.

evidence.runtimeObservation: Hunger decreases during normal Gauntlet gameplay and can affect sprint.
evidence.currentBehavior: Vitals are restored at setup/transition points but are not continuously normalized during the run.

notes.title: Add Explicit Final Victory Feedback
notes.problem: Tester runtime shows the completed Gauntlet run returns the player through the terminal flow without a dedicated final Win/Victory acknowledgement. The selected artifact does not provide enough evidence to classify this as a gameplay defect.
notes.action: If the intended UX requires explicit terminal acknowledgement, add one authoritative final victory/result notification after the run result is committed and before the lobby transition completes.

evidence.runtimeObservation: No dedicated final Win/Victory notification was observed at full-run completion.
evidence.sourceObservation: Level 15 completion presentation exists, while the whole-run terminal flow returns/reset players without a separate final victory surface.
